ledger.x: 16 February 1918: Lithuania is re-established as a state.
Autumn 1918: the kingdom gives way to a republic.
January 1919: the Lithuanian Taryba leaves Vilnius as Polish-Soviet clashes begin east of the city ('the Lithuanian Taryba left Vilnius'); the seat moves to Kaunas.
1920: Lithuania secures Vilnius from the Bolsheviks.
Autumn 1920: Poland takes the Vilnius area.
Autumn 1920: Vilnius passes to Zeligowski's Central Lithuania, a Polish-backed state.
24 March 1922: the dispute is settled in fact.
19 January 1923: the revolt ends in annexation.
19 January 1923: Lithuania annexes the Klaipeda Region (2,657 km2).
23 March 1939: Lithuania cedes Klaipeda to Germany.
10 October 1939: Lithuania receives Vilnius from the Soviet Union.
15 June 1940: the Soviet Union invades Lithuania.
21 July 1940: Lithuania's People's Seimas asks to join the Soviet Union, ending the Republic of Lithuania; the Supreme Soviet accepted 'in early August'.

wars.name: Polish-Lithuanian conflict over the Vilnius Region
wars.outcome: Lithuania held Vilnius briefly in 1920 and lost it to Zeligowski's mutiny in autumn 1920; Poland annexed the Vilnius Region on 24 March 1922; Lithuania did not recognise it.

wars.name: Klaipeda Revolt
wars.outcome: Lithuania occupied the territory and annexed it on 19 January 1923; the Conference of Ambassadors confirmed it in 1924 and the Klaipeda Convention of 8 May 1924 settled the autonomy.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of Lithuania
wars.outcome: Ultimatum of 14 June, invasion of 15 June, rigged elections of 14-15 July, request of 21 July and acceptance in early August 1940; no fighting.

certainty.note: The frontiers were not fixed: the Polish and Soviet fronts moved around Vilnius and the Suwalki area, and the Klaipeda Region was under League control.
